messages.author: 7a265b4b83a1c62a
messages.subject: Efficiency query for NIMBLE model
parts:
Hi,

I have an efficiency query about NIMBLE. I have a change-point survival model which I have successful fit. I want to make sure that I have optimized the computation of this model so I have a question about how functions are called for each set of sampling steps.

In the psuedo-code below I have change-points (cp) and parameters for the model (beta). I have to run a relatively intensive function to get my data into a "counting process" format (see survival SurvSplit for more details). Once I have my data in that format I evaluate the loglikelihood based on the parameters (beta). 

I would like to confirm that  "survSplit" is only run when proposing parameter values for cp and not reevaluated when proposing values for beta as X_mat remains the same for different values of beta.

If it is, is it possible to avoid this happening. 

Many thanks,
Philip  
#######
 
  mod <- nimbleCode({
    for(i in 1:ncp){
    cp[i] ~ ordered_uniform(0, 10)
   }
#Computationally intensive nimbleFunction
 X_mat <- survSplit(X, cp)   


    for(i in 1:ncovar){
    beta[i] ~ dnorm(0, 10)
   }
 #Actual evaluation of the (log) likelihood:
LL <- get_cpLL(X_mat, beta)
zero ~ dpois(-LL + C)
   
  })

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Efficiency query for NIMBLE model
parts:
Hi Philip,
That should be correct.
You can see what will be computed when updating a node such as "cp[1]" by entering model$getDependencies("cp[1]"), where model is what was returned from nimbleModel.
I'm puzzled about how your code could be working because you would need brackets such as "X_mat[1:a, 1:b] <- survSplit(X[1:a, 1:b], cp[1:ncp])" etc. where obviously I've made up the index ranges and assumed X and X_mat are matrices (alternatively you can have empty index spots if you have provided the dimensions argument to nimbleModel). Can you please clarify if this was working code you shared?
Here is a way you could verify: Run the mcmc uncompiled, with a browser or debug in the run code of survSplit. Then you'll be able to inspect each time it is called. You still will not be sure which sampler is operating when survSplit is called. To pin that down, you could build an MCMC with sampling only on the cp[i] nodes (or even only a single such as cp[1]), or only on the beta nodes or one of them (see nodes argument to configureMCMC or buildMCMC) and then see if survSplit is called by the resulting samplers (again, running uncompiled).
HTH
Perry
